# Page 22^page=22
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 22 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS NSO Released Publication “Energy Statistics India 2026” On March 30, 2026, the National Statistics Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), released the 33rd edition of its annual publication, “Energy Statistics India 2026″. • The report provides a comprehensive dataset on India’s energy reserves, capacity, production, and consumption and import/export of all the energy commodities, including: Coal, Lignite, Petroleum, Natural Gas (NG), Renewable Energy (RE), among others, of India, along with analytical tools like energy balance tables, sankey diagrams, and Sustainable Energy Indicators as per International Standards for the Financial Year 2024-25 (FY25). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of Energy Statistics India 2026 ✓ Released by: NSO, MoSPI ✓ Edition: 33rd ✓ Key Highlights: ✓ Rapid Growth in RE Potential: 47,04,043 MW (as of March 31, 2025) ✓ Major Sources of RE: Solar Energy (33,43,378 MW during FY25); Wind Power (11,63,856 MW) and Large Hydro (1,33,410 MW) ✓ Credit Flow: Rs 10,325 crore in 2025(6-times increase over 2021) ✓ Dominant Energy Source: Coal (5,52,315 KToE in FY25) ✓ Per-Capita Energy Consumption: 18,096 Mega Joule/person (1.89% CAGR) About Energy Statistics 2026: Coverage: This year, the publication has enhanced its’ coverage by including new features such as: • Data on credit flow to domestic energy-sectors, global energy-statistics etc.; • Detailed consumption patterns; • Electricity usage in industries based on the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) database; • Data on fuel consumption by aviation and marine sectors. Standardization: The publication standardizes end-use sectors consumption across all energy commodities to enhance data consistency. Key Highlights Surge in RE Potential: The publication highlighted a significant surge in India’s Renewable Energy (RE) potential, which stood at 47,04,043 MegaWatt (MW) as on March 31, 2025. • Among all the RE sources in India, Solar Energy dominated this segment, with a staggering growth of 33,43,378 MW (during FY: 2024-25) (around 71% of total potential); followed by Wind Power (11,63,856 MW) and Large Hydro (1,33,410 MW). Credit Flow: The publication revealed that the Credit Flow to the energy sector in India has increased more than 6-times i.e. from an amount of Rs 1,688 crore (in 2021) to Rs 10,325 crore (in 2025). TPES: During FY25, India’s Total Primary Energy Supply (TPES) registered a growth rate of 2.95%, which stood at 9,32,816 Kilo Tonnes of oil Equivalent (KToE). TFC: The Total Final Consumption (TFC) of energy, into different end-use sectors, surged by over 30.41 % i.e. from 4,69,212 KToE (in FY16) to 608,578 KToE (in FY25).

# Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF Per-Capita Energy Consumption: As per the publication, the per-capita energy consumption has increased from 15,296 Mega Joule/person (during FY16) to 18,096 Mega Joule/person (during FY25), registering Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 1.89% over the years. Dominant Energy Source: Among all the major energy supply sources, coal has remained the dominant source in India, with supply increasing from 3,87,761 KToE (in FY16) to 5,52,315 KToE (in FY25). Regional Concentration: The report noted that over 70% of India’s total potential for generation of RE is concentrated in six states viz. Rajasthan (23.70%), Maharashtra (14.26%), Gujarat (9.10%), Andhra Pradesh (9.1%), Karnataka (8.59%) and Madhya Pradesh (8.09%). Installed RE Capacity: The installed RE- capacity has registered a significant growth i.e. from 90,134 MW (as on March 31, 2016) to 2,29,346 MW (as on March 31, 2025), which is a CAGR of 10.93% over the years. Electricity generation from RE Resources: As per the publication, electricity generation from Resources (both Utility and Non-Utility together) has also increased from an amount of 1,89,314 Giga-Watt-Hour (GWH) (FY16) to 4,16,823 GWH (FY25), which is a CAGR of 9.17% over the years. Energy Loss: The publication showed reduction in the transmission and distribution losses, which was around 22% during FY16, compared to around 17% during FY25. About National Statistical Commission (NSC): Chairman- Rajeeva Laxman Karandikar Headquarters- New Delhi, Delhi Established – 2006 MeitY Approves 29 Projects Worth Rs 7,104 Crore under 4th Tranche of ECMS In March 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) approved 29 proposals under the 4th tranche of Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with a projected investment of Rs 7,104 crore and projected production of Rs 84,515 crore to generate 14,246 direct employment opportunities. • Following the earlier approval of 46 applications worth Rs. 54,567 crore, a total of 75 applications have now been approved under ECMS, with expected investments of Rs. 61,671 crore and direct employment for 65,040 people. Exam Hints: ✓ What? 4th tranche approvals of 29 projects under ECMS ✓ By Whom? MeitY ✓ Investment: Rs 7,104 crore ✓ Production: Rs 84,515 crore ✓ Employment: To generate 14,246 direct employment ✓ Target: USD 500 billion electronic ecosystem by 2030- 31. Approvals of Electronics Manufacturing: Coverage: Approvals span 16 products with cross-sectoral applications across mobile, telecom, consumer electronics, automotive, strategic electronics, and Information Technology (IT) hardware. Components: • 1 sub-assemblies: Display Modules • 11 bare components: Antennas, Capacitors, Connectors, Heat Sinks, Li-ion Cells, Relays, Resistors, Transducers, SMD Passives, Flexible PCB and Inductors

# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF • 3 supply chain items: Laminates, Metallized films for Capacitors and Rare Earth Permanent Magnets • Capital Goods and their parts Investment: Major investments include Rs.1,683 crore in capital goods (6 proposals) and Rs.1,350 crore in display module manufacturing (2 proposals). Milestone: The approvals include to establish India’s first Surface Mount Device (SMD) passive plant for tantalum capacitors in Andhra Pradesh (AP) by Syrma Group; • The first Flexible Printed Circuit Board (PCB) plant with budget of Rs. 588 crore in AP by Syrma Strategic Electronics (SSEPL) in partnership with South Korea’s Shinhyup Electronics; and • The first Rare Earth Permanent Magnet facility with budget of Rs. 700 crore in Uttar Pradesh (UP) by Lohum Cleantech. Priority Areas: The four core priorities for electronics manufacturing are strengthening in-house design capabilities through collaborations, building a robust domestic supply chain with support for indigenous capital equipment Significance: Enhances domestic value addition (DVA), reduces import dependence, strengthens the electronics manufacturing ecosystem, and promotes advanced manufacturing capabilities in India. About Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS): Background: Approved in April 2025 by the Government of India (GoI) with an outlay of Rs. 22,919 crore for Financial Year (FY) 2025–26 to FY32 (with a one-year gestation), later proposed to be enhanced to Rs. 40,000 crore. Objective: Develop a robust electronics component ecosystem by boosting Domestic Value Addition (DVA) and integrating with Global Value Chains (GVCs). Incentives: Provide support through turnover-linked, Capital Expenditure (Capex)-linked, and hybrid incentive structures. Target: Achieve a USD 500 billion domestic electronics manufacturing ecosystem by 2030–31. About Ministry of Electronic and Information Technology (MeitY): Union Minister- Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha member- Odisha) Minister of State (MoS)- Jitin Prasada (Constituency- Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, UP) PM E-DRIVE Subsidy Extended till July 31, 2026 for Electric Two-Wheelers In March 2026, the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) extended the demand subsidy for electric two- wheelers (e-2Ws) under the Prime Minister’s Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme till July 31, 2026, providing an additional four months beyond March 31, 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Extension of subsidy for electric two-wheelers ✓ Scheme: PM E-DRIVE Scheme ✓ Extended Till: 31 July 2026 ✓ Ministry: Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) ✓ Subsidy Rate: Rs 2,500 per kWh (max Rs 5,000/vehicle) ✓ Total Outlay: Rs 10,900 crore ✓ Launch: PM E-DRIVE Scheme launched in 2024 by MHI About Extension of PM E-DRIVE Scheme: Extension: Subsidy for e-2Ws overall scheme continues till 31 March 2028, with electric three-wheelers (e- 3Ws) supported throughout the scheme period. Outlay: Total allocation of Rs. 10,900 crore, including Rs. 3,679 crore for demand incentives and Rs. 7,171 crore for e-buses, charging infrastructure, and testing facilities.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 25 Daily Content PDF Incentive: Incentives are processed through the VAHAN (National Vehicle Registration) portal, offering Rs. 2,500 per kWh (kilowatt-hour) capped at Rs. 5,000 per vehicle for models priced up to Rs. 1.5 lakh to reduce upfront costs. About Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI): Union Minister – Haradanahalli Devegowda (HD) Kumaraswamy (Constituency- Mandya, Karnataka) Minister of State (MoS)– Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma (Constituency- Narasapuram, Andhra Pradesh, AP) CCRAS Signs MoU with Anuvadini AI to Translate Ayurveda Research into 13 Languages In March 2026, the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), under the Ministry of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy), signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Anuvadini AI, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) voice-to-voice translation platform, to translate evidence-based Ayurveda research accessible in 13 regional languages, including Hindi. • The MoU was signed by Professor Vaidya Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General (DG) of CCRAS, and Dr. Buddha Chandrasekhar, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Anuvadini AI. MoU signed for multilingual Ayurveda research access ✓ Entities: CCRAS, Ministry of AYUSH and Anuvadini AI, Ministry of Education ✓ Languages: 13 regional languages (including Hindi) ✓ Objective: Promote accessible Ayurveda knowledge About CCRAS–Anuvadini MoU: Objective: Expand access to evidence-based Ayurveda knowledge, overcome language barriers, and ensure equitable dissemination across India. Technology: Utilize AI-based translation by Anuvadini, developed by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) under Ministry of Education (MoE). Translation: CCRAS, the apex Ayurveda research body with 30 institutes across 25 states, will use AI to translate its research outputs, CCRAS Bulletin, and Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials into 13 regional languages for wider accessibility. DGCA and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya Signed MoU to Train Youth in Aviation In March 2026, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (GSV), Ministry of Railways (MoR) to enhance skill development in the aviation sector, including Aviation Engineering and Aviation Management. • The MoU was signed by Director General (DG) Faiz Ahmed Kidwai, DGCA and Vice Chancellor Professor Manoj Choudhury, GSV, in the presence of Union Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, MoCA and Ashwini Vaishnaw, MoR. Indian Air Force (IAF) ✓ Cost: Rs 1,950 crore ✓ Category: Buy (Indian–IDDM) ✓ Design: Indigenously designed by Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE) ✓ Manufactured by: BEL About the Mountain Radar System: Development: It was indigenously designed by Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE) under the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) to boost domestic defence capabilities. Interest rates on Small Savings Schemes kept unchanged ✓ Announced by: DEA-Budget Division, MoF ✓ Period: Q1FY27 (April 1, 2026 – June 30, 2026) ✓ Rates: KVP-7.5% (115 months), PPF-7.1%, SSY-8.2%, NSC-7.7%, SCSS-8.2%. ✓ Method: Recommended by Shyamala Gopinath Committee (January 2023) Overview of Post Office Savings Schemes: SSY: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) offers 8.2% interest, allows a guardian to open an account for a girl child below 10, with Rs. 250–Rs. 1,50,000 yearly deposits, Section 80C benefits, and Exempt-Exempt- Exempt (EEE) tax status (tax free). Review: Interest rates are reviewed quarterly since 2016 based on Government Securities (G-Sec) yields and market conditions, following Shyamala Gopinath Committee recommendations of 25–100 basis points (bps) higher rates. About Ministry of Finance (MoF): Union Minister- Nirmala Sitharaman (Rajya Sabha- Karnataka) Minister of State (MoS)- Pankaj Chaudhary (Constituency- Maharajganj, Uttar Pradesh, UP) RBI Extends Implementation of Revised CME framework to July 01, 2026 In March 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) extended the implementation of its revised Capital Market Exposure (CME) framework by another 3 months to July 01, 2026 (originally scheduled for April 01, 2026).

# Page 29^page=29
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF • In February 2026, RBI issued the final Amendment Directions on CME, aimed to provide an enabling framework for banks to finance acquisitions by Indian corporates; • Rationalize the limits for lending by banks to individuals against shares, units of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), among others, and introduce a principle-based framework for lending to Capital Market Intermediaries (CMIs). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Extension of timeline for implementation of revised CME framework ✓ Extended by: RBI ✓ New Timeline: from July 01, 2026 ✓ Previous Timeline: from April 01, 2026 ✓ Key Changes: ✓ Modified definition of Acquisition Finance: Includes Mergers and Amalgamations ✓ Loan Limits against Securities: Rs 1 crore per individual; Rs 25 lakh for IPO-related loans, FPOs and ESOP subscriptions Other Key Changes: Modified Definition of Acquisition Finance: RBI has also modified the definition of acquisition finance which now includes the mergers and amalgamations. RBI has further clarified that acquisition finance may be extended only to acquiring control over non-financial target companies. Other Key Changes for Acquisition Finance: If the target company is a holding company or parent company with control over other subsidiary companies, the criteria of ‘potential synergy’ is required to be collectively achieved for acquisition finance. • Banks have been mandated to get corporate guarantee from the acquiring company in cases of acquisition finance extended to a subsidiary or a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) of the acquiring company. Loans Against Securities: As per RBI directions, the new rules will now apply limits on loans against eligible securities across the banking system, restricting them at Rs 1 crore per individual and Rs 25 lakh for Initial Public Offering (IPO)-related loans, Follow-on-Public Offer (FPOs) and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) subscriptions.
